--- title: "Using the tidyr Package in R" date: "1/6/2025" date-modified: last-modified date-format: long --- # Tutorial: Using the tidyr Package in R ## Introduction ### Overview The `tidyr` package, part of the `tidyverse`, is designed for data tidying—reshaping data into a tidy format where each variable is a column, each observation is a row, and each value is a single cell. Key functions include: - `tidyr::pivot_longer()`: Reshape wide data into long format. - `tidyr::pivot_wider()`: Reshape long data into wide format. - `tidyr::separate()`: Split a column into multiple columns. - `tidyr::unite()`: Combine multiple columns into one. - `tidyr::drop_na()`: Remove rows with missing values. - `tidyr::replace_na()`: Replace missing values. ### Use Cases - Reshaping data for analysis or visualization. - Cleaning and preparing raw datasets. - Combining or splitting columns for better data structure. ### Benefits - Simplifies handling of messy or untidy data. - Ensures compatibility with other `tidyverse` tools. - Offers a consistent and intuitive syntax. ## Getting Started ### Loading the Package Load `tidyr` using `pacman::p_load()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load(tidyr) ``` ::: ### Basic Usage Reshape a simple dataset: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data <- data.frame( ID = 1:3, Gender = c("M", "F", "M"), Age_2022 = c(25, 30, 35), Age_2023 = c(26, 31, 36) ) # Pivot longer data |> tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Age"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Age") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| ID|Gender |Year | Age| |--:|:------|:--------|---:| | 1|M |Age_2022 | 25| | 1|M |Age_2023 | 26| | 2|F |Age_2022 | 30| | 2|F |Age_2023 | 31| | 3|M |Age_2022 | 35| | 3|M |Age_2023 | 36|
::: ::: ## Key Functions and Features ### tidyr::pivot_longer() #### Description Converts wide data into long format, making columns into rows. #### Syntax ```r tidyr::pivot_longer(data, cols, names_to, values_to, ...) ``` - `data`: A data frame. - `cols`: Columns to pivot. - `names_to`: Name of the new column for column names. - `values_to`: Name of the new column for values. #### Example ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data |> tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c(Age_2022, Age_2023), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Age") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| ID|Gender |Year | Age| |--:|:------|:--------|---:| | 1|M |Age_2022 | 25| | 1|M |Age_2023 | 26| | 2|F |Age_2022 | 30| | 2|F |Age_2023 | 31| | 3|M |Age_2022 | 35| | 3|M |Age_2023 | 36|
::: ::: ### tidyr::pivot_wider() #### Description Converts long data into wide format, making rows into columns. #### Syntax ```r tidyr::pivot_wider(data, names_from, values_from, ...) ``` - `data`: A data frame. - `names_from`: Column containing names for new columns. - `values_from`: Column containing values for new columns. #### Example ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} long_data <- data |> tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Age"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Age") long_data |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Year, values_from = Age) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| ID|Gender | Age_2022| Age_2023| |--:|:------|--------:|--------:| | 1|M | 25| 26| | 2|F | 30| 31| | 3|M | 35| 36|
::: ::: ### tidyr::separate() #### Description Splits a single column into multiple columns. #### Syntax ```r tidyr::separate(data, col, into, sep = " ") ``` - `data`: A data frame. - `col`: Column to split. - `into`: Vector of new column names. - `sep`: Separator to split on. #### Example ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data <- data.frame(Name = c("Alice_2022", "Bob_2023")) data |> tidyr::separate(Name, into = c("Name", "Year"), sep = "_") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|Name |Year | |:-----|:----| |Alice |2022 | |Bob |2023 |
::: ::: ### tidyr::unite() #### Description Combines multiple columns into one. #### Syntax ```r tidyr::unite(data, col, ..., sep = "_") ``` - `data`: A data frame. - `col`: Name of the new column. - `...`: Columns to combine. - `sep`: Separator between combined values. #### Example ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data <- data.frame(Name = c("Alice", "Bob"), Year = c(2022, 2023)) data |> tidyr::unite("Name_Year", Name, Year, sep = "_") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|Name_Year | |:----------| |Alice_2022 | |Bob_2023 |
::: ::: ## In-Depth Examples ### Example 1: Reshaping and Summarizing #### Objective Summarize the mean age by gender and year. #### Steps ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data <- data.frame( ID = 1:4, Gender = c("M", "F", "F", "M"), Age_2022 = c(25, 30, 27, 35), Age_2023 = c(26, 31, 28, 36) ) data_long <- data |> tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Age"), names_to = "Year", values_to = "Age") summary <- data_long |> dplyr::group_by(Gender, Year) |> dplyr::summarize(MeanAge = mean(Age), .groups = "drop") summary ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|Gender |Year | MeanAge| |:------|:--------|-------:| |F |Age_2022 | 28.5| |F |Age_2023 | 29.5| |M |Age_2022 | 30.0| |M |Age_2023 | 31.0|
::: ::: #### Output A summary table of mean ages by gender and year. ### Example 2: Combining and Cleaning Columns #### Objective Combine year and ID into a unique identifier. #### Steps ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data |> tidyr::unite("UniqueID", ID, starts_with("Age"), sep = "-") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|UniqueID |Gender | |:--------|:------| |1-25-26 |M | |2-30-31 |F | |3-27-28 |F | |4-35-36 |M |
::: ::: #### Output A new column `UniqueID` combines values. ## Advanced Features ### Customization #### Add Prefixes or Suffixes ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data_long |> dplyr::mutate(Year = paste0("Year_", Year)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| ID|Gender |Year | Age| |--:|:------|:-------------|---:| | 1|M |Year_Age_2022 | 25| | 1|M |Year_Age_2023 | 26| | 2|F |Year_Age_2022 | 30| | 2|F |Year_Age_2023 | 31| | 3|F |Year_Age_2022 | 27| | 3|F |Year_Age_2023 | 28| | 4|M |Year_Age_2022 | 35| | 4|M |Year_Age_2023 | 36|
::: ::: ### Integration Combine with `ggplot2` for visualization: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggplot2) data_long |> ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = Age, fill = Gender)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") + labs(title = "Age Distribution by Year", x = "Year", y = "Age") + theme_bw() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tidyr_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Optimization Tips - Use `select()` before pivoting to limit unnecessary columns. - Avoid excessive pivoting by designing data collection appropriately. ## Troubleshooting and FAQs ### Common Issues #### Error: Columns Must Be Unique Ensure column names are unique before pivoting. #### Warning: NA Introduced Check the data for inconsistencies or missing values. ### FAQs - **Can `tidyr` handle large datasets?** Yes, but consider chunking with `data.table` for very large data. - **How do I preserve column types?** Use `tidyr::pivot_longer()` or `pivot_wider()` with `values_transform`. ## Best Practices - Start with well-structured raw data. - Use descriptive column names and standard formats. - Avoid overusing `pivot_longer()` or `pivot_wider()` for reversible tasks. ## Conclusion ### Summary `tidyr` simplifies reshaping and tidying data with a cohesive set of functions. ### Next Steps Explore advanced tidying tasks with `tidyr` or integrate with other `tidyverse` tools like `ggplot2` and `dplyr`. ## References and Resources - [tidyr Documentation](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/) - [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/) - [Tidyverse GitHub](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyr)
